text:
Jada Williams: need to lock RBAC for model metadata + customer-facing changelog publishing. current draft is: anyone w/ registry write can update fields AND publish notes. enterprise folks will push back. can we align today?

Jordan Lee: yeah separation-of-duties is the big one. we should treat “edit metadata” and “publish customer-visible note” as different permissions.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. also: prod should not allow direct writes from personal accounts. ideally group-based (Okta) and service accounts for automation.

Dylan Brooks: what’s the minimum set of roles we need for v1? keep it simple but defensible.

Connor O'Brien: release eng POV: we need a clear “who can push the button” during freeze windows + emergency hotfix path. but agree it can’t be wide open.

Marissa Cole: product requirement: drafts can be created as part of model event ingestion, but publication must be gated (PM + release eng + support readiness). customers will ask “who approved this” in audits.

Marcus Lin: security lens: at minimum: (1) least privilege, (2) audit trail for every change + publication, (3) immutable history / no delete, (4) breakglass process logged.

Naomi Feldman: compliance: enterprises like FinchBank will ask for evidence of review/approval and retention. also they’ll want a named “approver role” that is not the same as editor.

Kevin Osei: and we need to be able to prove in logs: actor, role, source IP (if applicable), request id, and what fields changed. esp for “public fields”.

Quentin Harris: question: model metadata itself includes internal stuff (bench notes, vendor provenance, etc). we’re planning a public allowlist, right?

Jordan Lee: yup. PR idea is `public_changelog_fields` allowlist + enforced redaction. even if someone edits internal-only fields, generator should never emit them.

Ethan Park: how do we map that to permissions? e.g. should “metadata editor” be allowed to modify internal-only fields but not public fields?

Jada Williams: i was thinking:
- Role A: `model-metadata-editor` (edit registry records; can change non-public fields)
- Role B: `model-metadata-public-editor` (can change fields that can appear in customer notes, like compatibility, deprecation timeline)
- Role C: `model-changelog-approver` (can move draft -> in_review -> approved)
- Role D: `model-changelog-publisher` (can publish approved note to docs/feed)
Does that feel too many?

Dylan Brooks: 4 roles is ok if we make defaults sane. but i’d rather not split public vs non-public editor unless we have to.

Marcus Lin: splitting is actually useful. biggest risk is someone accidentally flipping a deprecation date or changing “replacement_model” and it ships externally.

Marissa Cole: also from UX: we want a clear “public-facing fields” section in Console. only certain folks should be able to edit those.

Connor O'Brien: +1 to splitting. release eng does not want random infra folks changing deprecation timelines the morning of a launch.

Dev Patel: support readiness angle: we want to require a support signoff for deprecations / behavior changes. at least a checklist + assigned approver. not necessarily a separate role but needs to be captured.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC implementation thought: keep roles but map to Okta groups:
- `okta:redwood-model-registry-editors`
- `okta:redwood-model-registry-public-editors`
- `okta:redwood-changelog-approvers`
- `okta:redwood-changelog-publishers`
And enforce in API gateway + service.

Jordan Lee: on workflow states: draft -> in_review -> published (and a “retracted/superseded” state, not delete). permissions:
- editors can create draft
- approvers can move draft <-> in_review + approve
- publishers can publish only if approved

Naomi Feldman: add requirement: approver != publisher for regulated tenants? or at least configurable. some customers will ask.

Ethan Park: do we need tenant-specific enforcement now? sounds like v2.

Marcus Lin: we can implement a platform default: approver and publisher can be same human, but we should strongly recommend separation. if we can log both steps, that helps.

Connor O'Brien: for emergency: we sometimes need to publish a correction fast (typo / wrong compat note). propose “hotfix publish” that still logs approval, but can be a smaller approver set (on-call).

Jada Williams: maybe:
- standard path requires 2-party: at least one in approvers AND one in publishers (can be different groups)
- emergency path: “breakglass” publisher can publish without approval but triggers pager + postmortem requirement

Kevin Osei: breakglass must generate an audit event + immutable retention. also alert to SIEM / #security-audit.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: + we should do it via dedicated endpoint requiring reason string. e.g. `POST /changelog/{id}/publish?mode=breakglass` w/ `reason="..."` logged.

Quentin Harris: for public edits, can we add validation requiring required sections? e.g. deprecation needs `sunset_date`, `replacement_model`, and customer messaging.

Marissa Cole: yes pls. also require “Compatibility” block always present in published note even if it’s “No change.” (docs team asked for consistency.)

Jordan Lee: summarizing proposed access matrix (v1):
- `model-metadata-editor`: edit internal fields (provenance notes, perf measurements, infra details)
- `model-metadata-public-editor`: edit public-facing fields (compat, context window, tool calling support, deprecation fields)
- `model-changelog-approver`: set status draft<->in_review, mark approved, add required checklist items
- `model-changelog-publisher`: publish approved entries + supersede (correction) + rollback w/ new entry
Breakglass: restricted to on-call release eng + security, requires reason, sends alert.

Dylan Brooks: works for me. action items: Jada/Jordan write this up in the RBAC section of schema+generator doc; Kaitlyn to confirm Okta group names; Kevin/Marcus to confirm audit fields.

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: and please ensure “who changed what” includes field-level diff for public fields at least.

Kevin Osei: + retention: we should state “no deletes; supersede only; retain for 7 years” (or whatever GRC signs off). will follow up.

Connor O'Brien: i’ll sync w/ release eng re: breakglass + freeze window constraints. don’t want this blocking RC publishes.

Jada Williams: cool. i’ll update workflow doc + ping in #product for approval semantics. thanks all.
